results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec
All 48 aligned units' summaries match the controlling ideas of p01-p48 in spec order; the three intro callout units are house-format apparatus outside the spec's paragraphs.
The outliner marked no unit as needing two summaries.

Every unit ties to a supporting claim S1-S5 through its section; the cross-border paragraph (Seller Balances ¶4) traces only weakly but is declared by the spec (s5 p3) and its thread problem is recorded under flow_is_followable.

results.draft_locus: Refunds and Chargebacks Against a Payment Already Split ¶5 (recovery table)
results.quote: Both providers document three ways to recover, with two limits.
results.finding: The recovery table is announced as three ways and two limits, but it has four rows (the fourth, 'Platform pays', is not a recovery), and the limits the prose names (Stripe's available-balance condition, Adyen's 30 days) are not the time limits the table's cells carry ('a transfer after 180 days'). No sentence after the table says what it shows; the spec's 'shows' (the same three ideas under different names, each with a documented time limit, 180 days on Stripe and 30 on Adyen) is never stated, and the 180-day cell is unexplained until When It Goes Wrong.

Other tables (three parties, Stripe charge types, Adyen split types, Stripe refunds, designs, provider differences, Larkfield ledger and comparison tables), Figures 1-3 with captions, and the quotations are each introduced or followed by a sentence saying what they show.

results.draft_locus: Seller Balances, Payout Schedules and Top-Ups ¶1
results.quote: On Stripe each connected account has a payout `interval` (manual, daily, weekly or monthly) and a delay.
results.finding: Declared cause_effect, carrying over 'reversals that find the balance empty' and introducing 'the schedule that empties it'. The section opens directly on Stripe configuration with no link to the reversals just discussed, so the reason the payout section follows reversals (the spec's flow rationale) is never expressed; both flow readers found the section's position unclear.

results.draft_locus: In Practice at Larkfield: Mila's €120 Three Ways, Then €84 Back ¶6
results.quote: That leaves the figure Femke asks for per studio.
results.finding: Declared conclusion_summary carrying over 'one payment's open half' and introducing 'the same quantity summed per studio'. The sentence instead points back to a request Femke never made (her three questions do not ask for a per-studio figure), so the known information it picks up does not exist in the text; both flow readers stopped here.

All other boundaries (intro p02-p04, scene, bookings, Stripe, Adyen, reversals, designs, comparison, worked example, failures, conclusion and hand-off) express the declared relationship and pick up the declared known information.

results.draft_locus: Seller Balances, Payout Schedules and Top-Ups (section position)
results.quote: On Stripe each connected account has a payout `interval` (manual, daily, weekly or monthly) and a delay.
results.finding: Both flow readers find the position of the payouts section after reversals unclear and propose moving it before the reversals section, following the payment's own timeline (payout 11 March, refund 18 March). The order also breaks the spec's own declared prerequisite_order ('each supplies the vocabulary the next uses'): the reversals section's recovery table already uses settlement netting and top-ups, which only the payouts section defines. The difficulty comes from the order itself, not only from the prose.
results.corroborated_by: r-flowB, section list item 'Seller Balances, Payout Schedules and Top-Ups' (position unclear) and Part 4 reorder (r-flowA: section list 'Partly unclear', Part 4 first reorder)

results.draft_locus: Stripe and Adyen: Where They Differ (section position)
results.quote: The table sets this chapter's documented facts side by side; the last column is my reading and is inference.
results.finding: Both flow readers find the provider comparison, placed after the designs section, reads as a step back/recap and would move it up next to the mechanics (r-flowA A15, r-flowB B9). The finding concerns only the position of a house-format section.

results.draft_locus: Adyen: Typed Bookings Declared With the Payment (table)
results.quote: `Interchange`, `SchemeFee`
results.finding: Interchange, scheme fee, blended pricing and Interchange++ appear in the table before the following paragraph explains them; minor as the explanation follows at once. Reported by one reader only.
Opens on a puzzling scenario (correct arithmetic, wrong books, €317,200) followed by the claim; none of the weak patterns.
Conclusion sorts findings by how settled they are, adds the author's synthesis and callback, introduces no new subtopic and holds no body evidence.

The synthesis that the charge type, splits list, chargeback logic and payout schedule answer one question in advance is stated by no single section, and the Larkfield bullet says why it matters (a leg-by-leg ledger and per-studio reconciliation would have shown each debit the day it happened).
'Larkfield's €317,200 was never lost. It was a set of debits to balances already paid out, for which Larkfield wrote no entry' returns to the €317,200 in the hook as the spec's callback requires.

The cold reader predicted every roadmap section in order (scene, bookings, Stripe/Adyen, reversals, payouts, three designs, provider comparison, worked example and failures), the evidence (scenario figures, dated provider documentation, comparison and ledger tables) and the practical, cautionary tone. Its uncertainties (the three designs unnamed, what the later comparison adds) do not contradict the roadmap.

The reader says the marketplace has paid (refund debits the balance booked through, platform-first/liable account), gives recovery by transfer reversal leaving the seller negative and netted against future sales, or a consented debit of the seller's bank, and names the record: each leg and the payout keyed to the payment with the provider's references so the refund can find what to reverse. Matches expected.

The reader answers no: the request validates only the format of the split, and a missing or closed balance account sends the whole amount and fees to the liable balance account without an error; reconcile per split against transfer webhooks and the Balance Platform Accounting Report. Matches expected.

In Practice: €117.47 to Studio Noord and €2.53 Commission, €0.61 processing cost labeled '(assumption)', payout Thursday 11 March, €84.00 refund on 18 March after it; consistent with the scenario ledger figures in the spec.
